subject: Furniture around fireplaces and alcoves
hook: Walls bend. Alcove units shouldn't leave a gap.
ig:
Walls bend. Alcove units shouldn't leave a gap. This is how we deal with it.

Most alcove walls in older homes bow, lean or both. A perfectly square unit pushed into a crooked alcove leaves a shadow line that you notice every time you walk past.

How we work:
1. Measure each alcove at several heights during the survey
2. Cut the unit to that alcove's own size in our Hanley workshop
3. Leave a filler on the wall side
4. On site, mark that filler to the shape of the wall
5. Trim it so the edge follows the wall, top to bottom

It's called scribing, and it's the difference between furniture that looks fitted and furniture that looks parked.

Planning alcove units? Comment ALCOVE and we'll send you the link to book a free design consultation.
fb:
Ever noticed a dark gap down the side of an alcove cupboard? That's a straight unit meeting a not-so-straight wall.

In this reel we show how we avoid it: measure the alcove at several heights, make the unit to size in our workshop, then mark and trim a filler on site so it follows the wall exactly. Joiners call it scribing.

If you've got alcoves either side of a chimney breast and want them to look properly built-in, we'd love to help.
